findings.evidence: R-20 (shouldAcquire) + R-21 (LEDGER_HISTORY 256): a candidate more than 256 ledgers behind the current ledger is not acquired unless minimumOnline covers it.
findings.title: A node that falls more than 256 ledgers behind cannot backfill the gap from peers

findings.evidence: R-18 (doAdvance sync gates): history fetch requires validated age under 1 minute, valid == published, write load under 8192.
findings.title: Backfill never runs while the node is behind; staying current always wins over catching up old history

findings.evidence: R-11 (sha512Half verification) + R-05 (header hash/sequence mismatch fails): integrity rests entirely on hash equality; fetch packs carry no signature and no peer authentication beyond the peer connection.
findings.title: Fetch-pack integrity rests on hash equality alone, with no signature on the contents

findings.evidence: R-02 (6 timeouts fail) + R-08 (5-minute reacquire block): a single ledger can be unacquirable for 5 minutes after 7 timeouts of 3 seconds.
findings.title: Six timeouts plus a five-minute reacquire block can stall one ledger for minutes

findings.evidence: R-13 (validated age over 40 s refuses fetch-pack builds): a behind or busy node cannot serve history, so fetch-pack load concentrates on the few in-sync peers.
findings.title: Stale or loaded nodes refuse to serve fetch packs, concentrating load on in-sync peers

findings.evidence: R-14 (512-object cap, 1-second build budget): a deep gap needs many fetch-pack round trips, one per up-to-512-object pack.
findings.title: The 512-object fetch-pack cap forces many round trips for deep history gaps

findings.evidence: R-12 (1-second staleness) + R-10 (45-second cache lifetime): fetch-pack requests and cached entries expire quickly, so slow peers contribute nothing.
findings.title: Fetch-pack requests expire after 1 second and cached entries after 45 seconds

findings.evidence: R-33 (getMissingNodes, 256 nodes per pass) + R-35 (neededHashes): a large state map needs many request rounds; each pass is capped at 256 missing nodes.
findings.title: SHAMap sync requests at most 256 missing nodes per pass

findings.evidence: R-17 (gotStaleData): nodes received for a finished acquire are stashed opportunistically and only hash-checked when used.
findings.title: Stale data is stashed unverified and only checked on later use

findings.evidence: R-37 (LEDGER_REPLAY defaults to false) + R-38 (replay task limits): replay is experimental and off by default, so it is not part of normal catch-up.
findings.title: Ledger replay is disabled by default and bounded when enabled

findings.evidence: R-32 (consensus-validated cache: 64 entries, 5 minutes): the window for built-vs-validated mismatch analysis is short.
findings.title: The consensus-validated cache keeps only 64 entries for 5 minutes

findings.evidence: R-26 (setFullLedger parent check) + R-30 (handleMismatch classification): a parent-hash mismatch invalidates prior ledgers one by one, walking backwards until the chain closes.
findings.title: A parent mismatch invalidates prior ledgers backwards until the chain closes
